title: Busy seasons
hook: new babies, deadlines, moves: shrink, don't stop, like Brother Lawrence turning the cake in the pan for love of God
tomorrow: too sick to move, a woman in bed saw visions. what did they say?

segments.voice: Yesterday's line: keep one thing. John of the Cross in the dry dark: not more force, and not leaving. Today the opposite problem. Not too flat. Too full.
screen: `KEEP ONE THING.` → `NOT TOO FLAT. TOO FULL.`

segments.voice: Pans clanging. Someone shouting an order. A sink full of dishes. That was Brother Lawrence's workplace. He was a lay brother in a Carmelite monastery in Paris, put to work in the kitchen, and he admitted he had a natural dislike for the job. Yet he told a visitor that, for him, the busy time in the kitchen, with several people calling for different things at once, was no different from the time of prayer.
screen: `PANS, ORDERS, DISHES.` → `A MONK WHO DISLIKED THE KITCHEN.` → `NO DIFFERENT FROM PRAYER.`

segments.voice: How? Not by finding extra hours. By shrinking prayer until it fit inside the work. His way has a name, and it became the title of the little book made from his talks and letters: The Practice of the Presence of God. Instead of waiting for a quiet hour, he turned to God with a word or a glance, again and again, in the middle of things. We can do little things for God, he said. He would turn the cake frying in the pan for love of God. A sizzle, a flip, a moment of attention, offered. He still kept the set times of prayer his order asked of him. He just refused to let the loud hours count as time away. That's the teaching his tradition passed on: in a busy season, prayer doesn't stop. It gets smaller, and it moves into the work. For a rule in a season of a new baby, a deadline or a move, Lawrence's way isn't to drop the practice until things calm down. It's to shrink it to something you can hold in one hand. A breath at the stove. One word at the sink. A small thing, done for love, in the middle of the noise.
screen: `SHRINK PRAYER TO FIT THE WORK.` · `THE PRACTICE OF THE PRESENCE OF GOD.` · `TURNING THE CAKE FOR LOVE OF GOD.` · `NO TIME COUNTS AS TIME AWAY.` · then, large: `SMALLER, NOT STOPPED.`

segments.voice: Pick up something from your day: a mug, a spoon, a pen. Turn it over slowly, once, the way Lawrence turned the cake in the pan, and name your busy-season version: what your practice shrinks to on the fullest day. For the rest of the sit, hold the object, and come back to its weight with each breath.
Busy seasons: the stretches when life is too full, when practice shrinks to fit inside the work, the way Brother Lawrence prayed at the stove.
Your line: smaller, not stopped. A flip of the pan can be a prayer. Day 1670, done in the middle of things.

howItsDone: Christians still read Brother Lawrence's The Practice of the Presence of God and try his way of turning to God briefly in the middle of work. On a personal rule, a busy-season version is a shrunken practice that fits a full day.
